patients.summary: Forty-year-old international business development manager with bipolar disorder on lithium and stage 3a CKD who joins in 2021. Lithium-era nephrogenic diabetes insipidus is found in 2024, then ciguatera on vacation, saline-induced hyperchloremic acidosis during home IV hydration in 2025, and Ebola virus disease after a 2026 work trip to Guinea, from which he recovers.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Summary of care, prior primary care office, sent at patient request ahead of transfer.

Patient: Dale Bradley, DOB 04/05/1981.

Problems:
1. Bipolar disorder. Lithium started 2019 by his psychiatrist at the time. Mood has been stable on it and he has had no episodes since. Once he was stable the psychiatrist handed prescribing back to us; we have refilled it since.
2. Chronic kidney disease. Creatinine 1.6 in 2020, 1.7 in spring 2021. eGFR around 50. No proteinuria on prior UA.
3. S/p appendectomy at 18.

Medications: lithium carbonate 300 mg capsule, 1 cap twice a day.
Allergies: NKDA.
Immunizations: COVID-19 Pfizer x2, April 2021. Tdap date not on file.
Family hx: father bipolar disorder; mother hypertension.
Social: never smoker, a few drinks a week, works in international business development.

Last lithium level 0.7 (spring 2021). TSH and calcium normal at that draw.

events.reason: New patient, establish care and physical

documents.title: New Patient Visit and Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient. 40M moving his care here after relocating to Haydenville. Records from his prior office reviewed before today.

He is here mostly to get established. Feels well. Works in international business development, on the road abroad several times a year. Sleeps fine, exercises a few times a week.

Bipolar disorder: on lithium since 2019, started by a psychiatrist; prior PCP had been refilling. Mood steady, no highs or lows he can remember in the last two years, no thoughts of self-harm. Takes it twice a day with meals and rarely misses. Happy to keep labs here.

Kidneys: knows he has 'reduced kidney function' — creatinine 1.6-1.7 on outside labs. No swelling, no urinary complaints.

PMH: bipolar disorder; CKD stage 3a. PSH: appendectomy at 18.
Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with bipolar disorder; mother with hypertension.
SH: never smoker, 2-3 drinks a week, no drug use. Single.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well-appearing, calm, good eye contact, organized thought. HEENT unremarkable. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, old RLQ scar. No edema. No tremor at rest or with arms outstretched. Skin clear.

A/P
1. Bipolar disorder, stable on lithium — continue 300 mg BID. Lithium level, TSH, calcium today, then every 6 months with kidney labs. PHQ-9 2.
2. CKD 3a — CMP, UA, urine albumin/creatinine. Avoid NSAIDs; told him why.
3. Health maintenance — lipids, A1c, one-time HIV and hep C screens. Tdap today (no date on file). COVID primary series done in April. Flu shot in the fall.

RTC 6 months for labs, 1 year for physical.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Tdap 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS given. Pt tolerated well, no reaction after 15 minutes.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Dale,

Your labs from Tuesday are in. Lithium level is in the target range. Kidney function is about where your old office had it (creatinine 1.7) — stable, and there's no protein in the urine, which is good. Thyroid, calcium, blood count, sugar and cholesterol all normal. HIV and hepatitis C screens negative.

No changes. We'll repeat the lithium and kidney labs in about six months.

— your primary care physician

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for flu vaccine before a work trip next week. Denies fever or illness today. Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Waited 15 min, fine.

documents.title: Booster
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got my COVID booster Saturday at the pharmacy (Pfizer). Sending a photo of the card for my record. Arm was sore that night, nothing else.

documents.title: RE: Booster
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Dale — added the 11/6 booster to your immunization record.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Trough lithium level in range. Creatinine steady at baseline, lytes and calcium normal. Continue current dose. Portal message sent.

documents.title: Refill before trip
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I'm leaving for two weeks overseas for work on the 20th and I'll run out of lithium while I'm gone. Can you send the 90-day refill early? Same pharmacy.

documents.title: RE: Refill before trip
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sent. The pharmacy may need to run a vacation override with your insurance — if they give you trouble, call us and we'll talk to them. Safe travels.

documents.title: Pharmacy call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy called — early fill of lithium rejected by insurer. Gave travel dates; pharmacy submitted vacation override and it went through. 90-day supply ready today. Pt notified by text.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Doing well. Busy year — trips to Europe and Asia, no illness on the road. Mood even; sleeping 7 hours. Lithium BID without missed doses. No tremor, no thirst or urinary change, no GI upset.

Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID. NKDA.
SH unchanged: never smoker, 2-3 drinks/week.

Exam: NAD. HEENT normal. Neck no thyromegaly. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. No edema. Neuro nonfocal, no tremor. Affect bright, appropriate.

PHQ-9 1.

A/P
- Bipolar disorder: stable. Continue lithium; level and TSH today.
- CKD 3a: CMP, UA, urine albumin/creatinine. Remains off NSAIDs.
- Prevention: hepatitis B series — Heplisav dose 1 today, dose 2 in a month with flu shot. Lipids today. Colon screening starts at 45.

RTC 1 year; labs again in about 6 months.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lithium therapeutic, TSH normal, creatinine at his baseline, lipids fine, urine albumin normal. No changes. Released to portal with a short note.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Three vaccines today per PCP plan. Feels well, no fever.
- Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM L deltoid
- Heplisav-B dose 2, 0.5 mL IM R deltoid (series complete)
- COVID-19 Pfizer bivalent 0.3 mL IM L deltoid, separate site
VIS given for each. Observed 15 min without reaction.
